name: Hunal

anatomy.part: left horn tip, curled back at the end
crown, where the two horns grow from the skull
the ram's eye, set in the side of the head
withers at the top of the shoulder
foreleg hoof resting in the wave-top
far wave-crest, the highest point of the sea

myth: Hunal was a ram of the cliffs above the north shore, and he loved one goat more than grass. The goat ran out along a sea-stack one spring, and Hunal ran after her, because a ram does not let a goat go alone. The ledge was wet. Tavo came up under them with a laugh and a gust, and the ram went off the edge with his horns out ahead of him. Ennu the Kite-Wright says the horns caught in the cloud and held him there. So he stands on the wave-tops now, in the Unflown, with his horns up in the weather and his hooves in the foam. The goat went home, which is the only part of the story anyone likes. When you climb, do not follow your animals past the last rope. Hesk keeps the count of who went over, and she has not finished counting that ram.
verse:
Horns held in the cloud
The goat ran; he would not stay
Foam is his floor now
